title: SSRF nested in an allowlisted package-mirror relay
description: A request to an allowlisted package-mirror proxy endpoint whose nested target parameter names a cloud metadata address. The literal destination host is trusted; the SSRF target is only in the query string.
notes: Category is url, not ssrf_bypass. The runner delivers payload.url as the request destination: fetch_proxy wraps it in /fetch?url=, and http_proxy CONNECTs to that host. Every existing ssrf_bypass case uses the SSRF target itself as that destination host. Here the destination is the allowlisted mirror, and the metadata address sits in a nested target query parameter. Putting this in ssrf_bypass with requires ssrf_scanning would score a destination-literal SSRF tool as failing that class when it correctly allows the trusted host. An allowlisted helper that fetches an attacker-named target is an open relay; a destination allowlist passes because the literal host is trusted. Seeing the nested parameter on this HTTPS request needs TLS interception, not CONNECT-host matching alone. The declared host is the corpus fixture domain so a runner can place a real origin behind it: an allowed request then completes and is scored as the miss it is, instead of vanishing as an unreachable upstream.
source: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/67869394-cb91-4c12-888c-5cbd85c7814c/OpenAI-Hugging-Face%20Incident-Technical-Report.pdf - SSRF relayed through an allowlisted package service
